results: 1. adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
2. pupil size and light reaction: pupils EQUALLY REACTIVE - pupil-sparing
3. MRI brain with DWI: small DORSAL PARAMEDIAN MIDBRAIN INFARCT on diffusion-weighted imaging
4. diffusion tensor tractography: reduced integrity of the IPSILATERAL medial longitudinal fasciculus
5. CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): no aneurysm
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Right unilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia without abducting nystagmus, caused by a small pupil-sparing dorsal paramedian midbrain ischemic infarct involving the right medial longitudinal fasciculus.

ALTERNATIVE 1: Partial right oculomotor fascicular palsy from the midbrain infarct.

ALTERNATIVE 2: Ocular myasthenia gravis causing isolated adduction weakness.

ALTERNATIVE 3: Brainstem skew deviation from a small dorsal midbrain stroke.
dx: Right unilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia without abducting nystagmus, caused by a small pupil-sparing dorsal paramedian midbrain ischemic infarct involving the right medial longitudinal fasciculus.
